issue.title: Enhance JBang Documentation with Configuration and Qute Template
issue.body:
The existing configuration section was not functional due to issue #30087. This commit addresses this by documenting alternative methods using `application.properties` or `application.yaml`, as recommended in issue #41739.

Additionally, integrating Qute templates was not straightforward. This commit adds a dedicated section to the JBang documentation, providing instructions on including and using Qute templates.

Fix #41740 
Relates to #41739

body: It doesn't work because we don't record system properties from the build system. See https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/78045ea67413518f7c77271d08a70d03d1fffbbd/core/deployment/src/main/java/io/quarkus/deployment/configuration/BuildTimeConfigurationReader.java#L1023-L1106

I think the best alternative is to expose a `setRuntimeProperties` in https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/342a88e2830eba14c958ddd4b48277445b30edf7/independent-projects/bootstrap/core/src/main/java/io/quarkus/bootstrap/app/QuarkusBootstrap.java#L305, that we can use for these cases.

It can probably help with https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/27996 and getting rid of other places where we use System properties.

issue.title: Always record configuration values coming from Runtime Properties
issue.body:
- Follow up for #30087

In #30087, we added an API to propagate runtime properties in the Quarkus Builder. This allows integrators (like JBang), to provide configuration for runtime.

This change will always record such properties in the Quarkus application. We had cases where if the supplied properties were in the `quarkus` namespace and not part of our Config, we would ignore those.
